domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, manager decision, and optional cancellation.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — request created but not yet submitted; editable by the employee
SUBMITTED — request sent for manager review; awaiting approval or rejection
APPROVED — manager has approved; balance has been deducted; terminal state (except cancellation)
REJECTED — manager has rejected; no balance impact; terminal state
CANCELLED — request withdrawn by employee; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored; terminal state

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Each policy governs how many days are granted, whether manager approval is required, and any notice-period constraints.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; governs new leave requests
INACTIVE — policy is disabled; does not apply to new requests but historical references remain valid

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining days for a specific policy within a fiscal year. Deductions occur on approval; restorations occur on cancellation of an approved request.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect for the current fiscal year; used for entitlement checks and deductions
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays is zero; no further leave of this type can be taken this fiscal year
CLOSED — fiscal year has ended; balance is archived and a new balance is created for the next year

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Employment status governs eligibility for leave applications. The managerId field establishes the approval hierarchy for leave requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — employee is currently employed and eligible to apply for leave
INACTIVE — employee is on extended absence (not terminated); leave applications are blocked
TERMINATED — employee is no longer with the organization; all leave access is revoked

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Carries leave-related notifications to employees and managers. Triggered by state transitions on LeaveRequest (submission, approval, rejection, cancellation) and LeaveBalance exhaustion.
lifecycle_states: PENDING — notification created but not yet delivered
READ — recipient has viewed the notification
ARCHIVED — notification is no longer shown in the active feed

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

business_rules: The number of leave days consumed by a request is calculated as: (endDate - startDate) + 1, inclusive of both start and end dates. This count is used for balance-sufficiency checks, balance deductions, balance restorations, and all reporting. The unit is calendar days. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest day count appears, not only here]
A LeaveRequest can only transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED if the requesting employee's employmentStatus is ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can only transition from SUBMITTED to APPROVED if the approver is the employee's manager (employee.managerId === approver.id) and the approver has the MANAGER role. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can only be APPROVED if the employee has an ACTIVE LeaveBalance for the corresponding policy with remainingDays >= the requested day count. If no ACTIVE balance exists for the policy and fiscal year, the request is rejected with an insufficient-balance reason. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — balance sufficiency appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the requested day count and remainingDays is decremented by the same amount. If remainingDays reaches 0, the balance transitions to EXHAUSTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — balance deduction appears, not only here]

When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by the requested day count and remainingDays is incremented by the same amount. If the balance was EXHAUSTED, it transitions back to ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation — balance restoration appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can transition from SUBMITTED to REJECTED only by the employee's manager. Rejection has no effect on LeaveBalance. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest rejection appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can transition to CANCELLED from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED states. Only the requesting employee may cancel. Cancellation from APPROVED triggers balance restoration. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation eligibility appears, not only here]

When a LeavePolicy has a non-null minimumNoticeDays, a LeaveRequest can only be SUBMITTED if (startDate - today) >= minimumNoticeDays, where the difference is measured in calendar days and today is excluded from the count. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy minimum notice appears, not only here]

An employee cannot have two LeaveRequests in SUBMITTED or APPROVED state whose date ranges overlap. Overlap is defined as: requestA.startDate <= requestB.endDate AND requestB.startDate <= requestA.endDate. DRAFT and REJECTED requests are excluded from overlap checks. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest overlap prevention appears, not only here]

A manager cannot approve their own LeaveRequest. If employee.managerId === employee.id (self-managed), the request must be escalated to the next level or handled by an HR role. At minimum, the system must reject self-approval attempts. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest self-approval prohibition appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest must have startDate <= endDate. Requests where startDate > endDate are invalid at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest date ordering appears, not only here]

A Notification must be created on each of these LeaveRequest state transitions: DRAFT→SUBMITTED (notify manager), SUBMITTED→APPROVED (notify employee), SUBMITTED→REJECTED (notify employee), any→CANCELLED (notify manager if previously SUBMITTED/APPROVED). Additionally, when a LeaveBalance transitions to EXHAUSTED, notify the employee. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Notification triggers appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced (for architectureMdUpdate)

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED); any non-terminal → CANCELLED. Terminal states: APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED.
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE (toggle by admin).
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (when remainingDays hits 0); ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED → CLOSED (fiscal-year rollover).
- **Employee**: ACTIVE → INACTIVE (extended absence); ACTIVE/INACTIVE → TERMINATED (employment ends).
- **Notification**: PENDING → SENT → READ → ARCHIVED.

## Key domain decisions

- Day count is inclusive: `(endDate - startDate) + 1` calendar days — applied uniformly across balance checks, deductions, restorations, and reporting.
- Balance deduction is atomic with approval; balance restoration is atomic with cancellation of an approved request.
- Overlap detection considers only SUBMITTED and APPROVED requests; DRAFT and REJECTED are excluded.
- Self-approval is prohibited; the system must reject it.
- Minimum notice is measured as `(startDate - today)` in calendar days, excluding today.
- Notifications are triggered on every meaningful state transition (submission, approval, rejection, cancellation, balance exhaustion).

## Open questions for chief architect

1. Fiscal year boundary definition (calendar vs configurable).
2. Cross-fiscal-year request handling (reject, split, or anchor to startDate's fiscal year).
3. Accrual model (upfront grant vs monthly accrual vs prorated).
4. Carry-over rules (forfeit vs cap at maxAccumulation).

open_questions.question: How is the fiscal year determined for LeaveBalance assignment? Is it calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), a company-specific fiscal year (e.g., Apr 1 – Mar 31), or configurable per policy?
open_questions.impact: Determines which LeaveBalance is checked and deducted when a request spans a fiscal-year boundary, and when balances are rolled over or archived.
candidate_options: Configurable per LeavePolicy with a fiscalYearStartMonth field
Company-wide configuration stored as a system setting

open_questions.question: What happens when a LeaveRequest spans two fiscal years (e.g., startDate in December, endDate in January)?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance-sufficiency checks, deduction logic, and fiscal-year boundary handling.
candidate_options: Requests spanning fiscal years are rejected at submission
The request is split across two balances (current and next fiscal year)
The entire request is deducted from the fiscal year containing the startDate

open_questions.question: How does accrual work for annual leave? Is the full entitlement granted upfront at the start of the fiscal year, or does it accrue over time?
open_questions.impact: Determines when remainingDays is updated and whether mid-year hires get prorated entitlement.
candidate_options: Annual leave accrues monthly at accrualRate days/month
Annual leave is granted in full at the start of the fiscal year
Accrual is prorated based on hire date for the first year

open_questions.question: Do unused leave days carry over to the next fiscal year, and if so, up to what limit?
open_questions.impact: Affects fiscal-year rollover logic and the maxAccumulation field's semantics.
candidate_options: Unused days carry over up to maxAccumulation
Unused days are forfeited at fiscal year end
